issues.description: ALTER TABLE OneOf is large; the shape suggests a table of (keyword pattern -> sub-grammar) instead.
issues.detail: The AlterTableStatementSegment is now a single OneOf with ~12 sibling sequences. The data here is a dispatch table keyed by leading keywords (ADD/DROP/ALTER/SET/REBUILD/RENAME). Lifting each branch to a named grammar (AlterTableAddSegment, AlterTableDropSegment, etc.) would make the structure self-evident and the branches independently testable.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar duplicates SignedSegmentGrammar+NumericLiteral pair instead of one signed-number rule.
issues.detail: The seed/increment pair is the same shape twice. A small named grammar like SignedNumericLiteralSegment (optional sign + numeric) used twice would replace two near-identical fragments with one. Composition, not repetition. Also avoids drift if signed literals are needed elsewhere (and they will be).

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepts NumericLiteral with no fixture covering it.
issues.detail: The OneOf added NumericLiteralSegment for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE but no test exercises a numeric LCID. Either add a one-line fixture (DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=1033) or drop the branch. Untested parser branches are cleverness without load-bearing use; Rule 1 of measuring applies here too.

issues.description: DROP COLUMN branch nests Delimited(Sequence(... Delimited(ColumnReference))), which parses but reads awkwardly.
issues.detail: The outer Delimited wraps a Sequence whose tail is itself Delimited(ColumnReferenceSegment). For the common case (DROP COLUMN a, COLUMN b) the outer comma loop is what matters; the inner Delimited covers DROP COLUMN a, b (no repeated keyword). Worth a comment, or split into two explicit branches so the grammar matches how T-SQL actually reads.

review.summary: The change is mostly small, well-targeted parser additions with fixtures for each new shape — exactly the right altitude for dialect work. The main structural smell is that AlterTableStatementSegment is now a single sprawling OneOf; the underlying data is a keyword-dispatched table and would read better as a handful of named sub-grammars. The identity sign handling repeats the same (sign?, number) pair twice where one named grammar would do. One added OneOf branch (numeric DEFAULT_LANGUAGE) ships without a fixture. Nothing blocking; ship after a quick cleanup pass or as a follow-up.
